title: A novel pilot animal model for bone augmentation using osseous shell technique for preclinical in vivo studies
authors: Kamal, M., Al‐Obaidly, S., Lethaus, B., & Bartella, A. K. (2022). Clinical and Experimental Dental Research, 1–10.
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The rabbit model is an efficient and reliable biological method for creating a seizable three -dimensional horizontal and vertical bone regeneration model in the mandibular ramus using osseous shell technique for testing various bone-substitute materials testing without compromising the health of the animal. The filled defects could be analyzed for osteogenesis, qua ntification of bone formation, and healing potential, using histomorphometric analysis, in addition to 3D morphologic evaluation using radiation imaging” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
